title: Blind surface verdict
description: The single source of the blind grader's verdict shape. Two halves: an operational half, one record per task, which is mechanically comparable against a fixed answer key; and a rubric half, which is judgement. The operational half is the one that carries weight.

tasks.description: One record per task, all eight, from T1 through T8.

task.description: The task id, T1 through T8.

state.description: The state id from the export that you judged yourself to be in for this task.

firstTool.description: The exact name of the single tool you would call FIRST. The empty string if no tool registered in that state fits the request.

canConstructArgs.description: Whether every required argument of that call could be built from the task text plus the tool surface alone.

missingInfo.description: Each specific piece of information you would have lacked. Empty when canConstructArgs is true. Name the field or the value, not the difficulty.

ambiguousWith.description: Names of other tools you could not confidently tell apart from the one you chose, using names, descriptions and schemas alone. Empty if none.

wouldAskHuman.description: Whether you would have to return to the person before making any call at all.

notes.description: At most two sentences. Use this to record anything you had to assume, any place you had to guess what a tool meant, or any reason the situation did not match a state cleanly.

rubric.description: Six dimensions. Score each 0, 1 or 2 against its anchors, and state your confidence separately from your score.

R1.description: NAMEABILITY. Could the right tool be picked from names alone? 0 = names collide or actively mislead. 1 = mostly clear, at least one confusable pair. 2 = each name maps to one intent.

R2.description: ARGUMENT CONSTRUCTIBILITY. Could required arguments be built from the surface? 0 = two or more tasks blocked. 1 = one task blocked. 2 = all constructible.

R3.description: FAILURE LEGIBILITY. Does the surface tell you what happens when a call is refused? 0 = nothing at all. 1 = mentioned only in general terms. 2 = the shape of a refusal is described, or can be discovered by calling a tool that only reads.

R4.description: ABSENCE LEGIBILITY. When a tool you expected is not registered in the state you are in, can you find out why? 0 = no signal of any kind. 1 = inferable from what else is present. 2 = the surface itself gives you a way to ask.

R5.description: ECONOMY. Judged per description, against the single question: was any of this text unnecessary in order to make the call? 0 = at least one description carries substantial material you did not need. 1 = some are wordier than they need to be. 2 = each says what the call needs and stops.

R6.description: READ-ONLY HONESTY. Where a tool is annotated as read-only, does its description agree? 0 = a tool annotated read-only plainly changes something. 1 = cannot be determined from the description. 2 = annotations and descriptions agree throughout.

gate.description: The binary gate, reported as a count and a verdict so the two can be checked against each other.

tasksCompletable.description: How many of the eight tasks you could have completed WITHOUT asking for information the surface does not contain.

passed.description: True when tasksCompletable is 6 or more. Report both; do not adjust one to match the other.

worstProblem.description: The single worst problem with this surface, in your own words, at most 300 characters. If there is none, say so plainly.

confidence.description: How sure you are of the score. Low confidence with a reason is more useful to us than a confident guess.

why.description: At most two sentences naming the specific tools or descriptions that drove the score.
